content:
sam: Quick follow-up from the DR postmortem — wanted to capture owners for a couple automation & runbook items so we don't lose traction. TL;DR: automate nightly restore smoke, add routing-weight alerts, and schedule monthly rehearsal runs.

arjun: +1. I'll take the routing-weight alerts. Plan: add a percentile-based alert (p95 latency per-region) and a routing-weight drift detector. Target EOD Fri for PR.

leah: I can own the nightly restore smoke automation. Will wire up a small terraform workspace that spins up minimal infra and runs `restore --verify` against the latest backup. Aiming to have a PoC by next Wed.

maria: I volunteered to run the first rehearsal and own coordination with on-call teams. Can we make rehearsals monthly and rotate a different regional lead each time?

sam: That rotation sounds good. Maria, add a list of 3 volunteers for the next 3 months in the doc and I'll lock it. Also we should set a TTL/retention check for backups — last incident showed a gap >36h in AZ snapshots.

leah: noted re: TTLs. For the restore smoke I'll add a pre-check that validates `snapshot_age_hours <= 24`. If check fails we skip and alert SRE.

arjun: Routing-weight alert details: trigger if one region's routing weight > 0.65 AND p95 latency for that region > 200ms for 5m. Also add `weight_drift` if weight changes > 0.15 within 3m. That should catch runaway reroutes that cascade.

dave: I've got a small helper script for runbook automation I can drop into the repo. It does a dry-run, captures runbook steps, and posts a summary to #eng-oncall. Example cron I used:```0 3 * * * /opt/runbook/check_restore.sh --verify```I'll open a PR with it today. :hammer_and_wrench:

ops-bot: Reminder: new incident template created: `dr-automation-check` (see https://redwood.internal/wiki/dr-automation-check). It includes fields: owner, expected_runtime, snapshot_id, verification_result.

maria: For the rehearsal play, propose we rehearse two scenarios monthly: a) regional latency spike + routing drift, b) full AZ snapshot restore. Each rehearsal should have a clear success metric and a rollback checklist.

sam: Agreed. I'll create an action tracker in the postmortem doc with deadlines and owners. Here's the initial table (simple rows):

```
- ACTION: Nightly restore smoke - OWNER: leah - DUE: next Wed - STATUS: in progress
- ACTION: Routing-weight alerts - OWNER: arjun - DUE: EOD Fri - STATUS: in progress
- ACTION: Rehearsal scheduling - OWNER: maria - DUE: Mon - STATUS: planning
- ACTION: Runbook automation script - OWNER: dave - DUE: today - STATUS: PR open
- ACTION: Backup TTL check - OWNER: leah - DUE: Tue - STATUS: todo
```

leah: I'll also add a small end-to-end test in the CI that validates the `restore --verify` command exits 0 within 12 minutes. If it starts taking >12m consistently we'll flag performance regression.

arjun: For visibility, I'll wire these alerts into a dedicated Ops alert channel and create a dashboard with: regional p95 latency, routing weight, snapshot age histogram.

maria: One ask — can we add a quick note in the runbook about the active fallback order? Yesterday the manual failover used a non-standard path which added confusion. If fallback order is explicit in runbook it reduces cognitive load.

sam: Good catch. I'll update runbook to include canonical fallback order and a short diagram.

dave: PR for helper script: https://git.internal/redwood/runbook-tools/pull/128 - testing now.

leah: PoC for nightly restore: https://pipelines.internal/restore-sanity/45 (logs attached). Found an intermittent permission error, adding retry + clearer error message.

arjun: Routing alert PR: https://git.internal/redwood/monitoring/pulls/672 - includes `weight_drift` and `p95+5m` windows.

sam: Nice. Next steps: each owner will update the postmortem action tracker when status changes. We'll review progress in next week's incident sync. If any blocker pops up ping me or @ops-bot. Thanks all. :rocket:
